content.text:
Two trade-offs of using UUIDv7 as a primary key:

(1) Its values are ordered by time, so inserts land near each other in the index. That is kinder to the database than fully random identifiers, but the key reveals roughly when each row was created.
(2) It is 128 bits wide, so keys and indexes take more space than a plain integer key.

input.text: [lane-ibis] A lease-based lock gives one holder the lock for a set time, after which it runs out and another holder may take it. This depends on every machine agreeing roughly what the time is. If the holder's clock runs slow, it thinks it still has the lock after others see it expire, so two holders act at once. If a checking machine's clock runs fast, it may free the lock too early. Either way the lock's promise of one holder at a time is broken.
